hypotheses.statement: Primes are the irreducible prediction errors of a multiplicative generative model: a hierarchical predictor whose levels are periodic divisibility predictors produces an error stream that is exactly the primes, and each error promotes a new level. Experiment: a self-growing sieve-hierarchy and its error statistics.

The prime density 1/ln n is an entropy-production rate: a predictor of the integer stream pays Landauer cost only for errors, so its dissipation per integer decays like 1/ln n. Experiment: measure bit-erasure per step of a budgeted predictor against a Cramer random twin of matched density.

The primon gas (energy log n, Z = zeta(beta)) is an environment whose pole at beta = 1 is a learnability transition: a learner with a factorized (Euler-product) model gains advantage over an unfactorized one that grows as beta -> 1. Experiment: learning curves across beta.

Coprimality is statistical independence: the Chinese remainder theorem makes coprime periodic channels independent, so precision can be allocated per channel without cross-talk; a thermodynamic cost is paid only for non-coprime overlap. Experiment: niche partitioning of periodic predictors under coprime vs non-coprime sources.

The asymmetry between cheap multiplication and costly factorization is an arrow of time for an inferring agent: generation is near-reversible, inference dissipates; predictive priors are what reduce the dissipation of inference. Experiment: operation-count cost of factor inference with and without temporal priors.

Sieving is cooling: each sieve level removes composite microstates, and the survivors are defects of an annealing schedule whose depth trades maintenance energy against residual error. Experiment: find the free-energy-optimal sieve depth under a per-level cost and compare the residual with the Mertens product.

Precision is temperature and should track arithmetic regularity: an agent that sets its inverse temperature from recent surprise will fluctuate with prime-gap statistics, differently from a Poisson-gap twin. Experiment: surprise-driven thermostat on a prime indicator stream vs Cramer stream.

Self-growing sieve hierarchy: level k is a periodic predictor with period p_k predicting 'composite'; an integer that no level predicts is a residual error and is promoted to a new level with that integer as its period. Each level costs c energy units per step.

lenses.name: Sieve ledger
lenses.rationale: Invented for this triplicate: account for which level absorbed each integer's prediction, so error promotion can be audited.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: per-integer record of which levels predicted it
lenses.transformation: tabulate absorbed/passed counts per level and depth
lenses.nullExpectation: in a Cramer twin levels absorb at the rate of their own density with no nesting
failureModes: off-by-one in level promotion makes composites levels
finite-N edge effects at small N
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: attributes error reduction to specific levels instead of reporting only totals

lenses.name: Landauer ledger
lenses.rationale: Price every stored or erased bit, turning prediction quality into dissipation.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: bit-level memory writes and erasures of the agent
lenses.transformation: sum kT ln 2 per erased bit per step
predictedSignals: dissipation ~ a / ln n with a depending on depth
lenses.nullExpectation: dissipation flat in n for an agent that learns nothing
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: a thermodynamic currency comparable across agents of different architectures

lenses.name: Cramer twin contrast
lenses.rationale: Invented: every observable is paired with a density-matched random-prime world to separate arithmetic structure from density alone.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: prime indicator stream and a Bernoulli(1/ln n) stream
lenses.transformation: compute each observable on both and take the difference
predictedSignals: nonzero differences only where divisibility structure is used
lenses.nullExpectation: zero difference for mechanisms that use only density
failureModes: twin not matched at small n
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: isolates what depends on arithmetic, not on density

lenses.name: Euler-mode spectrum
lenses.rationale: Invented: decompose the agent's error signal into per-prime residue channels (Fourier over Z/p for each p).
lenses.transformation: for each small prime p, the DFT of e_n over residues mod p
lenses.nullExpectation: correlated channels when moduli share factors
failureModes: too few samples for large p
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: tests independence claims (CRT) directly in the error signal

lenses.name: Divisor-lattice ecology
lenses.rationale: Invented: represent populations of period-agents on the divisor lattice with edges gcd > 1 as niche overlap.
lenses.transformation: build gcd-overlap graph; compute component and coexistence statistics
predictedSignals: coexistence count equals number of coprime source components
lenses.nullExpectation: coexistence count at chance for non-coprime sources
failureModes: mutation rate too high to reach equilibrium
budget too loose so all coexist
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: an ecological reading of CRT absent from single-agent lenses

lenses.name: Inversion-cost arrow
lenses.rationale: Measure forward (generate) vs inverse (infer) operation counts as an irreversibility index.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: operation counts of the generator and the inferring solver
lenses.transformation: ratio infer/generate per sample; conditioned on prior quality
lenses.nullExpectation: ratio independent of prior when factors are i.i.d.
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: gives a work-based metric of prediction quality

lenses.name: Log-scale resonance
lenses.rationale: Spectrum of error or thermostat signals as functions of log n.
lenses.sourceRepresentation: time series indexed by log n
lenses.transformation: resample on a log grid and compute the power spectrum
failureModes: window too short to resolve gamma_1
lenses.informationAddedBeyondExistingLenses: probes explicit-formula structure no other lens reaches

experiments.hypothesis: A self-growing sieve hierarchy with per-level cost c has a free-energy-optimal depth K*(c) whose residual error rate follows the Mertens product, and this depends on arithmetic structure, not on prime density.
experiments.mechanism: levels = periodic 'composite' predictors; an unpredicted integer is promoted to a new level; cost per step = c * depth + (1 bit per residual error)
experiments.intervention: sweep c over {0.001, 0.003, 0.01, 0.03, 0.1}; cap depth at K and sweep K in 1..40
experiments.control: same agent with depth frozen at 0 (predict prime-density only)
experiments.positive_control: stream built as an explicit OR of periodic sources of periods {2,3,5,7}: depth must stop at 4 with zero residual
experiments.observable: residual error rate r(K) over n in [2, 10^5]; total cost per step; K*(c)
experiments.success_criterion: max relative deviation |r(K) - prod_{p<=p_K}(1-1/p)| / prod <= 0.05 for K in 1..20 on the real stream, AND on the null twin the ratio r(K)/r(0) at K=20 is >= 0.9
experiments.failure_criterion: relative deviation > 0.05 for any K <= 20 on the real stream, OR the twin achieves r(20)/r(0) < 0.9 (structure not arithmetic)
experiments.alternative_explanation: the sieve itself explains everything; the predictive-coding framing adds nothing beyond Eratosthenes
experiments.null_twin: Cramer stream: each n >= 3 labelled 'prime' with probability 1/ln n independently (matched density, divisibility structure destroyed); the agent runs unchanged
experiments.why_this_implementation: integers and periodic masks are the native objects; no learned function approximator needed
experiments.size: N = 10^5 integers, K up to 40 levels, 5 cost values, 10 seeds for the twin
stupid_explanations: the promotion rule is literally the sieve so success is guaranteed by construction
Mertens agreement is a known theorem, not a property of the agent
the Cramer twin fails because random streams are unpredictable by any periodic model, which says nothing about predictive coding

experiments.hypothesis: Under a truncated primon-gas environment the held-out log-loss advantage of a factorized (per-prime Bernoulli) learner over an unfactorized learner with equal parameter count grows as beta -> 1.
experiments.mechanism: Euler-product independence of divisibility events makes per-prime channels exact sufficient statistics
experiments.control: unfactorized learner: histogram over log-magnitude buckets with Laplace smoothing, parameter count matched to the factorized learner (number of primes <= 1000 = 168)
experiments.positive_control: an explicitly product-form synthetic world: independent geometric exponents per prime, which must show the factorized advantage at every beta
experiments.observable: held-out log-loss (nats per sample) on 5000 samples; gap G(beta) = loss_unfact - loss_fact
experiments.success_criterion: at T=1000, G(1.05) >= 2 * G(3.0) on the primon world (mean over 10 seeds, one-sided Welch p < 0.01), AND on the null twin G(1.05) <= 1.2 * G(3.0)
experiments.failure_criterion: G(1.05) < 2 * G(3.0) on the primon world, or the null twin shows the same ratio (>= 2)
experiments.alternative_explanation: heavier tails at low beta favour any model with explicit tail parameters, factorized or not
experiments.null_twin: magnitude-matched world: draw n from the primon law, then replace n with a uniformly random integer in the same dyadic bucket [2^k, 2^(k+1)); size law preserved, factor independence destroyed
experiments.why_this_implementation: direct sampling of integers with exact factorization by a precomputed smallest-prime-factor table; counting estimators suffice, no neural network
experiments.size: integers <= 10^6, 168 prime channels, 5 beta values, 3 T values, 10 seeds
stupid_explanations: truncation at 10^6 dominates behaviour near beta = 1
the matched-parameter histogram is simply a poor model
log-loss differences come from smoothing constants

experiments.hypothesis: Under an energy budget, a population of periodic predictors facing a superposition of coprime periodic sources sustains one distinct surviving period per source; with non-coprime sources of matched total density fewer periods coexist.
experiments.mechanism: reward for correctly predicted events is shared among agents predicting the same event; cost per agent per step proportional to 1/period; Boltzmann reproduction at temperature T; multiplicative mutation (x or / by 2,3,5,7)
experiments.intervention: coprime sources {3,5,7,11} vs non-coprime sources {4,6,10,12}; T in {0.1, 0.3, 1.0}
experiments.control: same population with reward not shared (no niche competition)
experiments.positive_control: a single source of period 5: exactly one period (5 or a multiple) must dominate
experiments.observable: number D of distinct periods with abundance >= 5% at step 20000
experiments.success_criterion: coprime world median D over 20 seeds in [3,5] AND non-coprime world median D <= 2, at T = 0.3
experiments.failure_criterion: coprime median D outside [3,5], or non-coprime median D >= 3
experiments.alternative_explanation: overlapping events in the non-coprime world simply reduce total available reward, shrinking the population
experiments.null_twin: non-coprime source set {4,6,10,12} with OR-combined event density matched to the coprime set within 2% (adjusted by dropping events at random)
experiments.why_this_implementation: an explicit agent ecology with integer genomes keeps the divisor lattice visible; an RL policy would hide period structure in weights
experiments.size: 64 agents, periods 2..60, 20000 steps, 20 seeds, 2 worlds, 3 temperatures
stupid_explanations: survivors merely copy the source periods, so coprimality of survivors is inherited not selected
density matching by random dropping adds noise that reduces coexistence
population size, not niche structure, limits D

experiments.hypothesis: The ratio of inference work (trial-division factoring) to generation work (one multiplication) falls with the temporal predictability of hidden factors when the solver uses a predictive prior ordering of candidate divisors.
experiments.mechanism: semiprime stream n_t = p_t q_t with p_t, q_t random walks over the prime index; solver tries divisors in order of prior probability from recent factors
experiments.intervention: prior-ordered trial division vs ascending trial division; walk step size s in {1, 3, 10}
experiments.positive_control: constant factors (s = 0): prior-ordered solver must succeed on first try for >= 99% of samples
experiments.observable: mean number of trial divisions per sample
experiments.success_criterion: on the drift world with s = 1, mean prior-ordered cost <= 0.5 x ascending cost; on the null twin prior-ordered cost >= 0.9 x ascending cost
experiments.alternative_explanation: memoization of the last answer, not prediction, produces the saving
experiments.null_twin: same marginal distribution of (p, q) as the drift world but temporally shuffled: magnitudes matched, temporal predictability destroyed
experiments.why_this_implementation: operation counts on a deterministic solver are an exact, cheap proxy for work; no learned model
experiments.size: primes < 10^4 (1229), 10000 samples per condition, 3 step sizes, 5 seeds
stupid_explanations: any cache beats no cache on a slowly varying stream
operation count ignores the cost of maintaining the prior
the asymmetry is a property of trial division, not of factoring in general

anomalies.text: shuffled null twin still favors the prior (R_null=0.186 < 1); see TREATMENT rows' range_idx_p/q for the index band the s=1 walk occupied
